quizzes.stem: A nightly job sends one request per report to a model with a one-million context window. The reports run up to about 650,000 words and are accepted. After the vendor moves the job to Claude Opus 5.5, which has the same window, the largest reports fail with "prompt is too long". The reports have not changed. What is the most likely cause?

options.a: The newer tokenizer turns identical prose into noticeably more tokens than before
options.b: Earlier requests in the same batch are kept and slowly fill the window over time
options.c: The output cap is now added into the size check before any request can be accepted
options.d: Always-on thinking now fills part of the window before the input is even counted

explanation.a: Claude Opus 4.7 and later cut text with a newer tokenizer that yields about 30 percent more tokens for the same text, and 1M tokens is roughly 555k words on it against about 750k earlier, so a 650,000-word report fit before and does not now (the tokenizers section).
explanation.c: Ruled out because on Claude 4.5 models and newer an input plus an output cap beyond the window is not refused: "the request is still accepted" (the limit section).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the API keeps no state between requests, and "your code resends the whole history on every request" (the stateless section).
explanation.d: Ruled out because the "prompt is too long" error is the input-only check: "If the input alone exceeds the window" the API refuses it, so output and thinking cannot be the cause (the limit section).

quizzes.stem: A support chat built on the Messages API passes only the customer's latest question to the model. The customer gave an order number two exchanges ago, and the assistant now asks for it again. Which change fixes this at the right layer?

options.a: Add a system line telling the model to remember each customer who sends a message
options.b: Move to the model with the largest context window that is available
options.c: Keep the dialogue in the application and replay it with every call
options.d: Raise `max_tokens` so the assistant can hold earlier details of the chat

explanation.c: The API remembers nothing, so memory is the history your code sends again with each request (the scripted pair of requests).
explanation.a: Ruled out because a model sees only what the request carries, and without the earlier messages "the model has no order number to talk about"; a system line adds no history.
explanation.b: Ruled out because each turn's input is "all previous conversation history plus the current user message", so a larger window holds nothing that was never sent.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "max_tokens is a cap on output, not on context", so raising it holds no earlier details.

quizzes.stem: A ticket router asks Claude to put each support ticket into one category. In testing, the same ticket lands in "billing" on one run and "account" on the next, though the prompt never changes. Which change best addresses the cause?

options.a: Append a line telling the model that a repeated ticket must get the same category
options.b: Have the reply pick one name from an enumerated set, and reject others in code
options.c: Set the temperature to zero and treat the output as fixed
options.d: Compare three runs and keep whichever category wins the vote

explanation.b: Variation comes from sampling and infrastructure (the sampling section), so a sentence cannot remove it; narrowing what the model may output and checking it in code can.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a prompt line "can make a behaviour much more likely; it cannot make it certain" (the steerability section).
explanation.c: Ruled out because the glossary warns that "even with temperature set to 0, the results will not be fully deterministic", and the current models reject any non-default value anyway (the sampling section).
explanation.d: Ruled out because comparing runs only reveals the variation: "Comparing detects the variation; it does not remove it" (the hallucination list).

quizzes.stem: A refund bot's requests carry just a tone guide and the customer's question. It states firmly that refunds are allowed for 45 days, while the real policy says 30. What best explains the firm wrong answer?

options.a: Its reliable knowledge cutoff predates the policy, so the answer is stale
options.b: It drew an unlikely number at sampling, so a second run would correct it
options.c: It recalled the company's own figure from its training, as its firm tone shows
options.d: It produced a typical-sounding number because nothing supplied the true one

explanation.d: The requests carry no policy, and a company policy is private material, unknown to the model unless it is placed in the context, so a plausible figure is a likely continuation (the hallucination section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because the knowledge section says "anything private (your tickets, your policies), is unknown to it" whatever the cutoff, so a cutoff date does not decide this.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a company policy "is unknown to it unless you supply it in the context or give it a tool that fetches it", and these requests do neither, while "confidence is not evidence", so the firm tone says nothing about where the figure came from.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a plausible-looking fact is a likely continuation whether or not it is true", so the invented figure is a likely pick rather than an unlucky draw, and a second run can give it again.

quizzes.stem: A team runs two assistants on Claude Sonnet 5.5: one drafts campaign slogans and the other reads amounts off bills. The lead wants the slogans varied and the amounts exact, and plans to tune each assistant's randomness separately through request settings. What actually happens?

options.a: Anything but the defaults comes back as a 400 error, so correctness has to be enforced by checks in code
options.b: Each assistant takes its own value, so slogan variety and amount accuracy can be tuned independently
options.c: Zero is accepted for the amounts assistant and then makes every output come out identical
options.d: Only top_p stays adjustable, so slogans can still be varied through that one setting

explanation.a: Claude Sonnet 5.5, like Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, rejects any non-default temperature, top_p or top_k with an error, so exactness for the bills comes from restricting and validating the output, and the slogans need no extra setting (the sampling section).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Messages reference says "all other values will be rejected", so no assistant can take a value of its own.
explanation.c: Ruled out because even where a zero is accepted, "even with temperature set to 0, the results will not be fully deterministic", and these models reject it.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the migration guide names all three parameters: "Omit temperature, top_p, and top_k, or leave them at their defaults: any other value is rejected".

quizzes.stem: A team plans to cut wrong answers by running every prompt three times and comparing the replies. It budgets the cost from what a token-counting tool reported for Claude Haiku 4.5. After the job moves to Claude Opus 5.5 the bill is about a third above budget, although the run count is as planned. Which earlier step would have given a sound budget?

options.a: Counting on Haiku 4.5 plus a small margin, since counts are only estimates
options.b: Dropping the comparison runs, since every extra run is another paid request
options.c: Querying the endpoint for the target model, since splits change by generation
options.d: Setting max_tokens low, so output cost cannot exceed the plan

explanation.c: The token counting endpoint returns an estimate against the model you name, and the same text yields about 30 percent more tokens from Opus 4.7 on, so a count made for the model the job moves to would have shown the rise (page 1, tokens are not words).
explanation.b: Ruled out because the run count was already budgeted and the bill still rose: "the same text produces about 30 percent more tokens than on earlier models", so the cost moved with the model and not with the runs.
explanation.a: Ruled out because an estimate "might differ by a small amount", while here the tokenizer itself changed, which is why the page says to "recount against the model you plan to use" rather than pad an old count.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "max_tokens is a cap on output, not on context", and the input side is where the new tokenizer adds tokens.

quizzes.stem: A scheduling assistant is asked to book "next Friday" mid-conversation and proposes a day from its training period. Which fix sits at the right layer?

options.a: Switch to the newest model, whose cutoff is closest to today
options.b: Have the application put the current calendar date in every request
options.c: Add a prompt line telling it never to guess the current day
options.d: Let it reason step by step about which date is meant before it proposes one

explanation.b: The model has no clock, so the date has to be supplied in the context on every call (the knowledge section).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Knowledge comes from training data with a cut-off", so even the newest model stops before today.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a prompt shapes the distribution and that is "why it is only a request", so a line cannot supply a fact the model lacks.
explanation.d: Ruled out because questions about today's date are "answered from stale or absent knowledge unless the context supplies the facts", so reasoning longer adds no date to work from.

quizzes.stem: A long contract is pasted into a request. The overview Claude returns cites a clause number that does not appear in the contract. Which prompt change most directly targets this failure?

options.a: Have it summarise each part on its own first, then join the parts into one overview
options.b: Ask Claude to state its confidence level beside each citation
options.c: Tell it to be an honest assistant that cites only clauses that really exist in the text
options.d: Have it first copy the relevant passages out exactly, then write only from them

explanation.d: Grounding the work in exact passages first means every claim can be traced to text that exists, which is the documented technique for long documents (the hallucination list).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a plausible-looking fact is a likely continuation whether or not it is true", so a summary of each part can invent a clause just as a single overview can.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "confidence is not evidence".
explanation.c: Ruled out because honesty is "a goal of training and not a guarantee of any single answer", so asking for it does not ground the citations.
